Taylor R.: Pinging the SDK folks 60; reproducible: RuntimeError: Event loop is closed when a notebook or pytest exits after using AsyncClient. Stack points at an atexit handler trying to run_until_complete().

Nina P.: that's our old auto-close behavior. We registered an atexit handler to avoid leaked TCP connections but run_until_complete() is unsafe if another loop owns the thread.

Omar H.: quick repro (notebook): create client at top-level, await client.embed(...), then restart kernel -> traceback during interpreter shutdown. Python 3.11, httpx 0.24.x, sdk 0.9.x.

Taylor R.: workaround for now: always use `async with AsyncClient(...)` or call `await client.aclose()` in teardown. But we need a proper fix in SDK.

Nina P.: proposed fix: remove blocking atexit handler; make finalizer non-blocking and idempotent. Implementation idea: use weakref.finalize to register a function that logs a warning (no loop work). In __del__ try: loop = asyncio.get_running_loop(); loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.create_task, self.aclose()) except RuntimeError: logger.warning("AsyncClient destroyed outside running loop; please call client.aclose()")

Omar H.: also update typing stubs so `async with AsyncClient()` is accepted by linters. Add examples in onboarding for notebooks, pytest-asyncio, and FastAPI lifespan.

Taylor R.: please add a regression test that simulates pytest-asyncio teardown and a short notebook-like flow. We should fail CI on tests that trigger run_until_complete from finalizers.

Infra Bot: Issue #2401 created: "python-async: remove run_until_complete from atexit; safe async finalizers + typing/docs" (labels: sdk, bug, docs)

Nina P.: assigning to @omar_h for patch and to @nina_p for docs + stubs. Will include migration note: implicit auto-close at process exit is deprecated; call aclose() or use async context manager.

Taylor R.: thanks! small change but saves a lot of noisy tracebacks in notebooks. :thumbsup:
